bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: There is no general quantitative restriction on bringing foreign currencies into China. Under Current Account Guide (Huifa〔2020〕14) Art. 89, inward passengers must make a written Customs declaration if carrying foreign-currency cash exceeding the equivalent of USD 5,000 (超过等值5000美元) — strictly exceeding, not '>=' — a declaration trigger, not an import ceiling. Art. 89 further provides that for same-day repeated travellers and short-interval repeated travellers, the second and subsequent entries require written Customs declaration regardless of the amount of foreign-currency cash carried (当天多次往返及短期内多次往返者第二次及以上入境，不论携带外币现钞的金额大小，均应向海关书面申报); that special rule is kept distinct from the ordinary > USD 5,000 threshold and is not expanded into a second headline numeric figure. Passengers intending later to take the same cash out should obtain the Customs-endorsed declaration record used for outbound release. Physical RMB cash is separate: PBOC Announcement〔2004〕No. 18 adjusts the national-currency carriage limit to CNY 20,000 per person per entry/exit under the State Council Measures for the Administration of the Entry and Exit of National Currency (State Council Order No. 108); Customs guidance applies 人民币现钞超过20000元 as a red-channel/declaration condition, with the exceeding part prohibited as a carriage limit. Negotiable instruments / payment instruments are not collapsed into this foreign-cash declaration threshold under Huifa〔2003〕102.

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out
take_foreign_currency_out.text: Outbound foreign-currency cash follows a layered SAFE/Customs architecture distinct from inbound declaration. Huifa〔2003〕102 and Current Account Guide Art. 89 are reconciled, not treated as competing regimes: (1) carrying foreign-currency cash not exceeding the equivalent of USD 5,000 (不超过等值5000美元（含5000美元）) generally requires no Permit for Carrying Foreign Exchange Abroad (携带证), and Customs releases; (2) where the traveller has no latest inbound foreign-cash declaration record, or carries more than that recorded amount, amounts above USD 5,000 up to and including USD 10,000 (等值5000美元以上至1万美元（含） / 5000美元以上至10000美元（含）) require a bank-issued 携带证, which Customs verifies on exit (Art. 89; Huifa〔2003〕102); (3) amounts above USD 10,000 may in principle not be carried (原则上不得携带超过等值10000美元), subject to specifically provided exceptional SAFE permit cases (Art. 89 identifies exceptional destination/need cases for SAFE 携带证; Huifa〔2003〕102 enumerates special-case pathways). Physical RMB cash remains a separate CNY 20,000 carriage limit under PBOC Announcement〔2004〕No. 18. This architecture is not a single symmetric USD 5,000 entry-and-exit declaration threshold and is not a universal USD 10,000 export ceiling. Customs listing of foreign-cash declaration conditions in both directions does not replace the outbound permit tiers.

cash_declaration_threshold.label: Declaration threshold
cash_declaration_threshold.text: China does not have one simple symmetric cash-declaration figure. Three distinct border regimes apply and must not be collapsed: (1) inbound foreign-currency cash — Current Account Guide Art. 89 written Customs declaration when the amount exceeds (超过) the equivalent of USD 5,000; declaration trigger, not an import ceiling; repeated same-day/short-interval second-and-subsequent entries require declaration regardless of amount under Art. 89 (bounded qualification, not a second ordinary threshold); (2) outbound foreign-currency cash — layered carriage/permit architecture under Huifa〔2003〕102 reconciled with Art. 89 inbound-declaration linkage: ≤ USD 5,000 equivalent (含) generally no 携带证; > USD 5,000 and ≤ USD 10,000 bank 携带证 where no/insufficient inbound record; > USD 10,000 in principle not carried except specifically provided SAFE permit cases; (3) physical RMB cash — separate CNY 20,000 per-person, per-entry/exit carriage limit set by PBOC Announcement〔2004〕No. 18 under the State Council national-currency carriage framework (Order No. 108), with Customs applying 人民币现钞超过20000元 as a declaration/red-channel condition. Huifa〔2003〕102 foreign-currency cash rules are not extended here to foreign payment instruments or securities. Enforcement sits with Chinese Customs; SAFE sets the FX cash-carriage administrative framework jointly with Customs.

exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: China's reviewed official sources do not establish a single general foreign-exchange authorisation regime. Distinct layers apply and must not be conflated: (i) a PBOC managed floating RMB exchange-rate regime based on market supply and demand with reference to a currency basket — a monetary fact kept separate from SAFE administration; (ii) current international payments and transfers not generally restricted, subject to genuine/lawful basis and bank authenticity/consistency review; (iii) capital-account FX handling that is transaction-specific (bank handling, registration, reporting, account/permitted-use controls, quotas, or approval where expressly required), including under the Capital Project FX Business Guide (2024) and subsequent 2025 cross-border investment/financing reforms; (iv) individual FX annual convenience amounts and account rules; and (v) Customs-enforced physical-cash declaration and carriage rules (foreign cash and RMB separately). Absence of a located restriction is not evidence that none exists.

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Domestic individuals (境内个人) may open FX savings accounts at banks on presentation of valid identity documents (Individual FX Measures Art. 32: 个人可以凭本人有效身份证件在银行开立外汇储蓄账户). Individual FX Measures Art. 2 distinguishes domestic vs overseas individuals and current vs capital individual FX; Art. 9 subjects individual settlement (结汇) and domestic-individual purchase (境内个人购汇) to annual total management. The current annual convenience amount (便利化额度) under the implementing rules / 2026 SAFE guidance is the equivalent of USD 50,000 per person per year for each of those categories. Within the convenience amount, transactions are handled at banks on identity documents; genuine current-account transactions outside the convenience amount may proceed with identity documents plus transaction-purpose evidence — the USD 50,000 figure is not asserted as a foreign-currency holding ceiling, bank-balance cap, universal remittance ceiling, universal transaction ceiling, or capital-account allowance. Purchased FX may, under the implementing rules, be remitted abroad, deposited into the individual's FX savings account, or carried abroad subject to the separate physical-cash rules. Outward current-account remittance from an FX savings account and hand-carried cash remittance follow their own documentary thresholds and are kept distinct from the convenience amount and from capital-account items (Individual FX Measures Ch. 3).

non_resident_rules.label: Non-resident rules
non_resident_rules.text: The reviewed sources distinguish overseas individuals (境外个人) from overseas institutions and do not support a comparative claim that non-residents 'transfer funds more freely'. Overseas individuals may open FX savings accounts on valid identity documents (Individual FX Measures Art. 32); current-account outward remittance of FX held in a savings account is handled at banks on identity documents under the implementing rules, while hand-carried foreign cash follows separate documentary thresholds. Overseas institutions legally established abroad may open domestic FX accounts under Huifa〔2009〕29: Art. 3 — domestic banks review overseas incorporation/registration documents, and except where SAFE otherwise provides, account opening does not require SAFE/branch approval; Art. 4 — accounts are labelled NRA (NON-RESIDENT ACCOUNT); Art. 5 — FX receipts/payments between domestic institutions/individuals and NRA accounts are managed as cross-border transactions, with banks reviewing applicable valid commercial documents; Art. 6 — NRA accounts may receive funds from inside/outside China, transfer between NRA accounts, transfer with offshore accounts, and pay outward, and domestic banks may process based on customer instructions unless SAFE provides otherwise (not an unrestricted-transfer entitlement); Art. 7 — balance-of-payments statistical reporting applies; Art. 8 — without approval of the competent SAFE branch/department, foreign-currency cash may not be deposited into or withdrawn from NRA accounts, and NRA funds may not be directly or indirectly settled into RMB. This is not a blanket entitlement to every banking product, and institutional NRA rules are not generalised here to all non-residents.

declaration.note: Inbound FX cash > USD 5,000 (超过等值5000美元, strictly '>', never '>=') is a Customs declaration trigger, not an import ceiling. Art. 89 also imposes a special regardless-of-amount written-declaration rule for same-day / short-interval second-and-subsequent inbound entries; that repeated-entry rule is a bounded qualification, NOT a second ordinary numeric threshold record. Customs may list > USD 5,000 declaration conditions in both directions, but the outbound legal architecture is not symmetric with inbound: outbound FX preserves ≤ USD 5,000 (generally no 携带证) / > USD 5,000–≤ USD 10,000 (bank-issued 携带证 where applicable) / > USD 10,000 (in principle not carried except specified SAFE permit cases), and outbound treatment depends where applicable on the latest inbound declaration record. Physical RMB CNY 20,000 is a separate carriage limit (PBOC Announcement〔2004〕No. 18 / State Council Order No. 108). Negotiable/payment instruments are not silently folded into Huifa〔2003〕102 foreign-cash thresholds. The USD 50,000 individual annual 便利化额度 is NOT a border-cash threshold and must not be read from this declaration block.

bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: Law 194/2020 Art. 213 (Official Gazette / NIB PDF p. 106) provides that bringing foreign currency into Egypt is guaranteed for all arrivals. There is no general quantitative inbound import ceiling in Art. 213. Disclosure on the prescribed form is required when the amount exceeds USD 10,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies (Arabic: إذا جاوز عشرة آلاف دولار — strictly 'exceeds' / 'جاوز', not '>=' / 'USD 10,000 or more'). Exactly USD 10,000 is outside this Art. 213 inbound disclosure trigger. This Art. 213 inbound limb addresses foreign currency (نقد أجنبي) only. Separately, AML Law 80/2002 Art. 12 and Exec Reg Art. 14(3) require customs disclosure when the value of foreign currency, bearer negotiable instruments, or both combined exceeds USD 10,000 equivalent (تجاوز / >) — an AML customs-disclosure layer, not an Art. 213 import ceiling and not a reason to fold BNI into Art. 213.

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out
take_foreign_currency_out.text: Outbound foreign-currency cash under Law 194/2020 Art. 213 (Official Gazette / NIB PDF pp. 106–107) is not symmetric with inbound. Ordinary departure rule: foreign currency may be taken out provided it does not exceed USD 10,000 or equivalent (Arabic: بشرط ألا يزيد على عشرة آلاف دولار — ordinary physical-carriage ceiling, operator <=). Separate exception: at departure, travellers may carry what remains of amounts previously disclosed upon arrival even where that remainder exceeds USD 10,000 (Art. 213 applies this remainder to travellers generally for FX). Separately, AML Exec Reg Art. 14(4) requires outbound customs disclosure when foreign currency, BNI, or both combined exceed USD 5,000 equivalent — a disclosure threshold distinct from the Art. 213 FX carriage ceiling, expressly without prejudice to the banking-law carriage architecture. Do not publish a symmetric 'USD 10,000 declaration at entry and exit'. Postal conveyance of Egyptian or foreign cash by letters/parcels is prohibited under Art. 213 and Exec Reg Art. 14(6). Physical EGP banknotes remain a separate Board-limit regime (Decision 2200/2020).

cash_declaration_threshold.text: Keep layers separate. (A) Law 194 Art. 213 FX cash: inbound disclosure when FX exceeds USD 10,000 (جاوز / >); no general inbound FX ceiling; outbound ordinary FX carriage <= USD 10,000 plus previously-disclosed inbound remainder exception. (C) EGP physical banknotes: Decision 2200/2020 Art. 1 — carriage within five thousand EGP entering or leaving (carriage ceiling, not a declaration threshold); Exec Reg Art. 14(5) also caps EGP banknotes or BNI at five thousand EGP. (D) BNI: defined in Exec Reg Art. 1; entry/exit treatment under Art. 12 / Art. 14 — not Art. 213 FX semantics. Do not collapse these into one symmetric USD 10,000 entry/exit figure.

exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Egypt's current architecture is not usefully summarised as legacy 'managed float with resident capital controls / largely liberalised current account'. The statute and current CBE monetary evidence establish: (i) market-determined EGP rate by supply and demand under Board FX-market rules (Art. 211), reinforced by the 6 March 2024 Special MPC market-forces decision and current 2026 monetary reporting; (ii) a broad Art. 212 right to retain FX and transfer inward/outward through licensed channels under Board procedures; (iii) a domestic EGP settlement default; (iv) dual traveller-cash layers — Art. 213 FX carriage/disclosure plus AML Art. 12 / Exec Reg Art. 14 FX+BNI customs disclosure (including outbound AML disclosure > USD 5,000); and (v) Arts 214–215 licensed multi-channel FX market supervision. On existing Passage Check taxonomy the exchange-control posture is floating_regulated_market: a market-determined exchange-rate framework with FX retention and inward/outward transfers through licensed channels, while domestic EGP settlement rules, licensed-market supervision and separate AML/cross-border cash controls remain operative — not a free float, not 'no exchange controls', and not a claim of fully liberalised or unregulated convertibility.

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Law 194/2020 Art. 212 (Official Gazette / NIB PDF p. 106) establishes that every natural or legal person may retain, own or possess foreign currency accruing to, owned by or held by that person, and may conduct foreign-exchange operations including inward and outward transfers, through banks or other entities licensed under the Law, according to rules and procedures set by the CBE Board. Pinpoint CBE currentness sweep located no residency-specific overlay that restores a general resident FX-holding authorisation requirement. Art. 212 is an eligibility / channel architecture, not a guaranteed entitlement to every bank product or account type, and not permission to deal outside licensed channels. Domestic transactions inside Egypt must be in EGP unless an international agreement, another law, or a Board-authorised case provides otherwise — a domestic settlement rule kept separate from international transfer rights.

bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: Cash and/or bearer payment instruments (cheques, traveller's cheques, promissory notes, bills of exchange), in Rupiah or foreign currency, with a total value reaching or exceeding IDR 100,000,000 (or the equivalent in another currency), must be declared to Indonesian Customs (Bea Cukai) on arrival via the applicable Customs Declaration channel (the All Indonesia integrated declaration for air and sea arrivals, and the Bea Cukai e-CD for land-border arrivals), under Government Regulation 99/2016. Where the cash brought in is Rupiah of IDR 100,000,000 or more, its authenticity is examined by Customs. Foreign banknotes (Uang Kertas Asing, UKA) with a value of IDR 1,000,000,000 or more may be carried into the customs area only by Bank Indonesia-authorised entities (banks and licensed non-bank money changers), not by ordinary individuals, under BI Regulation 19/7/PBI/2017 as amended. Below these thresholds the reviewed sources establish no declaration or permission requirement.

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out
take_foreign_currency_out.text: On departure the same IDR 100,000,000 customs declaration duty applies to cash and bearer payment instruments in Rupiah or foreign currency (Government Regulation 99/2016), filed through the Bea Cukai electronic Customs Declaration (e-CD), which is the channel Bea Cukai designates for outbound cash declarations. Physically carrying Rupiah banknotes of IDR 100,000,000 or more out of Indonesia additionally requires prior Bank Indonesia permission, a licensing requirement distinct from and not symmetric with the inbound treatment (inbound Rupiah of that amount is instead subject to a Customs authenticity examination). Carrying foreign banknotes (UKA) of IDR 1,000,000,000 or more out of the customs area is restricted to Bank Indonesia-authorised entities (BI Regulation 19/7/PBI/2017 as amended). The reviewed sources do not establish a separate general cap on the amount of foreign currency an individual may take out beyond these declaration and carriage rules.

cash_declaration_threshold.label: Declaration threshold
cash_declaration_threshold.text: The declaration threshold is a total value that reaches or exceeds IDR 100,000,000 (or the equivalent in another currency) in cash and/or bearer payment instruments, in Rupiah or foreign currency, for a traveller entering or leaving Indonesia (Government Regulation 99/2016), declared to Bea Cukai through the applicable Customs Declaration channel (the All Indonesia integrated declaration for air and sea arrivals; the Bea Cukai e-CD for land-border arrivals and for outbound cash declarations). Failure to declare carries an administrative fine of 10% of the amount carried, up to a maximum of IDR 300,000,000, to the extent established by the reviewed sources. This customs / anti-money-laundering border declaration is distinct from the Bank Indonesia Rupiah-carriage and foreign-banknote (UKA) carriage licensing regimes and from the DHE SDA export-proceeds regime, and it is not a currency import or export cap.

exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Indonesia does not operate a single general exchange-control authorisation regime in the reviewed sources; instead several distinct, layered regimes apply and must not be conflated: a customs declaration of cash and bearer instruments at or above IDR 100,000,000 (Government Regulation 99/2016); Bank Indonesia licensing and permission for physically carrying Rupiah banknotes (outbound of IDR 100,000,000 or more requires Bank Indonesia permission, while inbound of that amount is subject to a Customs authenticity examination) and foreign banknotes / UKA (IDR 1,000,000,000 or more restricted to authorised entities, BI Regulation 19/7/PBI/2017 as amended); the domestic Rupiah-use obligation with statutory exceptions (BI Regulation 17/3/PBI/2015); the DHE SDA export-proceeds retention and placement regime for natural-resource exporters (Government Regulation 36/2023 as amended through Government Regulation 21/2026); and foreign-exchange-market restrictions on Rupiah transactions with non-residents (BI Regulation 18/19/PBI/2016; BI Regulation 24/7/PBI/2022). The reviewed sources do not establish a general requirement of Bank Indonesia approval for capital transfers by residents, and they do not establish that Indonesia is 'fully liberalised' or has 'no controls'; absence of a located restriction is not evidence that none exists, and transaction-specific rules may apply.

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Residents (Penduduk) may hold and use foreign currency, while transactions conducted within Indonesian territory are generally required to be in Rupiah subject to statutory exceptions, including foreign-currency banking activities (BI Regulation 17/3/PBI/2015; statutory basis Law 7/2011 on Currency). The reviewed sources establish the Rupiah-use obligation and its exceptions but do not establish a general Bank Indonesia approval or quantitative limit on residents holding or operating foreign-currency accounts; the earlier on-file statement that residents face general BI limits or approval requirements for foreign-currency accounts is not supported by the located sources and is not asserted. Opening and operating bank accounts, including foreign-currency accounts, is governed by the general commercial-bank account-management rules (OJK Regulation POJK 24/2025) and by customer due diligence / know-your-customer under OJK Regulation POJK 8/2023; these govern the account-opening and account-administration process rather than establishing a residency-based entitlement. Under Indonesia's free-foreign-exchange framework (Law No. 24/1999), residents may hold and use foreign exchange, but the account-opening claim is not broadened beyond the located banking evidence, and account eligibility is not generalised beyond that evidence.

non_resident_rules.label: Non-resident rules
non_resident_rules.text: Non-residents (Bukan Penduduk) are subject to specific Bank Indonesia foreign-exchange-market restrictions in respect of Rupiah, including restrictions on Rupiah transfers abroad and on the provision of Rupiah credit or financing to non-residents, and limits on certain Rupiah transactions with non-residents (BI Regulation 18/19/PBI/2016; BI Regulation 24/7/PBI/2022 on the foreign-exchange market), subject to exceptions Bank Indonesia may allow. These are transaction- and market-level restrictions and do not by themselves establish a general non-resident bank-account-opening entitlement or prohibition. Account opening remains subject to the general commercial-bank account-management rules (OJK Regulation POJK 24/2025) and to customer due diligence / KYC (OJK Regulation POJK 8/2023). The located OJK sources prescribe customer-identification documentation, including foreign-citizen (Warga Negara Asing, WNA) documentation where applicable, but do not establish a general account-opening entitlement or prohibition based solely on Bank Indonesia resident/non-resident (Bukan Penduduk) status; foreign-citizen (WNA) status is a nationality concept and is not treated as synonymous with the BI non-resident (Bukan Penduduk) residency/economic-status concept. Account eligibility for non-residents therefore remains deliberately bounded and is not generalised beyond the located evidence. The earlier on-file claim that non-residents may transfer funds 'more freely' is not supported and is not asserted.

banking_conversion_practicality.label: Banking & channels
banking_conversion_practicality.text: Foreign-exchange conversion is available through banks authorised to conduct foreign-exchange activities and through licensed non-bank money changers (Kegiatan Usaha Penukaran Valuta Asing Bukan Bank, KUPVA Bukan Bank), which require a Bank Indonesia licence and are limited to authorised foreign-banknote exchange and related activities (BI Regulation 18/20/PBI/2016). Any conditions or limits Bank Indonesia applies specifically to money changers are particular to those licensees and are not general limits on bank customers. Documentation and underlying-transaction requirements may apply to larger foreign-exchange transactions, and the availability of a particular currency, service or rate is not guaranteed by any institution.

bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: Cash of EUR 10,000 or more brought into Italy must be declared to the Italian customs authority (ADM) at the first border customs office. Where the traveller enters the European Union through Italy the obligation arises under Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1672; where the traveller enters Italian national territory from another EU Member State it arises under Article 3 of Legislative Decree 195/2008. 'Cash' includes currency, bearer-negotiable instruments and gold used as a highly liquid store of value.

take_foreign_currency_out.text: Cash of EUR 10,000 or more taken out of Italy must be declared to the Italian customs authority (ADM) at the first border customs office. The obligation applies on leaving the European Union through Italy (Article 3, Regulation (EU) 2018/1672) and on leaving Italian national territory towards another EU Member State (Article 3, Legislative Decree 195/2008). The same cash categories apply; a declaration with inexact or incomplete information does not satisfy the obligation.

cash_declaration_threshold.label: Declaration threshold
cash_declaration_threshold.text: The threshold for a mandatory declaration of accompanied cash carried by a traveller is EUR 10,000 or more. Two parallel regimes apply and are administered through a single ADM declaration form: Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 for cash entering or leaving the European Union, and Article 3 of Legislative Decree 195/2008 for cash entering or leaving Italian national territory (including to and from other EU Member States). Unaccompanied cash sent by post, freight or courier is covered separately by Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 (disclosure on the request of customs). Customs may require production of the cash and apply administrative seizure; specific penalty amounts are fixed by Legislative Decree 195/2008.

exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Italy maintains no national exchange-control regime for capital movements or payments. Under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, all restrictions on the movement of capital and on payments, between Member States and with third countries, are prohibited. This is not unconditional: the Treaty preserves exceptions, including measures on taxation and the prudential supervision of financial services and declaration procedures for administrative or statistical purposes (Article 65), the option to maintain certain restrictions on direct investment involving third countries (Article 64), and temporary safeguard measures (Article 66), alongside EU restrictive measures (sanctions). This capital-movement framework is separate from the EUR 10,000 cross-border cash-declaration regimes.

bring_foreign_currency_in.text: A traveller entering Mexico must file a mandatory customs declaration when the means of payment carried — cash, national or foreign checks, payment orders or any other collectible document, or a combination — exceed the equivalent of USD 10,000 in total (Ley Aduanera, Article 9), on the official form approved by the SAT. cash_declaration_threshold.label: Declaration threshold

It is a mandatory report to the customs authorities (ANAM) on the SAT-approved form, triggered only above USD 10,000; failure to declare carries a fine of 20% to 40% of the excess (Article 185, fracción VII). exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Mexico's foreign-exchange regime is free-floating and set by the Comisión de Cambios — the SHCP and Banco de México — under Article 21 of the Ley del Banco de México; the Comisión determines the exchange-rate regime and Banco de México sets the rules for determining the exchange rate (Ley Monetaria, Article 8). The reviewed official sources do not establish a general authorisation, permission or approval regime for buying, holding or transferring currency; this reflects the limits of the sources reviewed, not a positive finding that no sectoral or capital-movement restriction exists. The operative restrictions identified are of a different character and are kept distinct — anti-money-laundering controls and quantitative limits on US-dollar cash operations (Ley de Instituciones de Crédito, Article 115), the customs border declaration (Ley Aduanera, Article 9), and AML reporting. Whether any narrower sectoral or capital-movement restriction exists outside the reviewed sources is not established either way.

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Under Banco de México Circular 3/2012, credit institutions may open peso (national-currency) deposit accounts to both natural and legal persons, with the lowest-tier and special-savings accounts reserved for natural persons. The reviewed official sources do not establish an unrestricted right for any resident to hold a foreign-currency (US-dollar) account: foreign-currency sight deposits payable in Mexico are available only to defined categories — natural persons domiciled in the northern 20-kilometre border strip or in Baja California and Baja California Sur, legal persons domiciled in national territory, and official representations of foreign governments and international organisations — while US-dollar transfer (SPID) accounts are opened only to legal persons domiciled in national territory. Banks also apply anti-money-laundering monitoring and reporting requirements to foreign-currency cash operations, together with quantitative daily and monthly limits on US-dollar cash operations for individual users differentiated by nationality, under the general provisions for Article 115 of the Ley de Instituciones de Crédito. Account opening remains subject to AML/KYC and each institution's own conditions; eligibility does not guarantee that any particular account will be opened.

non_resident_rules.label: Non-resident rules
non_resident_rules.text: The reviewed official sources do not establish a general entitlement for non-residents to hold foreign-currency accounts in Mexico: eligibility for foreign-currency sight deposits and for US-dollar transfer (SPID) accounts is tied to domicile in national territory, so non-resident persons generally fall outside these categories, aside from official representations of foreign governments and international organisations. A separate peso-denominated deposit and prepaid-card regime exists for Mexican nationals whose place of residence is abroad. US-dollar cash operations are additionally subject to anti-money-laundering controls and to quantitative limits for individual users differentiated by nationality under Article 115 of the Ley de Instituciones de Crédito. Account opening remains subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer screening and each institution's requirements; there is no entitlement to any particular account or service.

bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: IGOC 2026 Art. 36 permits resident and non-resident natural persons to import foreign-currency payment instruments and bearer negotiable instruments without a quantitative import ceiling. Art. 37 then requires Customs declaration at entry when effects of commerce, means of payment and bearer negotiable financial instruments have a value equal to or greater than MAD 100,000 (>=; égale ou supérieure) — not merely '>'. Below MAD 100,000, declaration is facultative. Office des Changes FAQ and Art. 37 further require presentation of the import declaration to justify origin for funding eligible FX/convertible-dirham accounts, re-export of the currencies, or where repatriated banknotes constitute export proceeds of goods/services — regardless of amount. The declaration is valid up to one month for residents and six months for non-residents and must be annotated by the bank for amounts collected. This is a declaration architecture, not an import ceiling, and is not Art. 42's physical-MAD banknote rule.

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out
take_foreign_currency_out.text: Outbound FX is residency- and source-specific under IGOC 2026 Art. 40. Resident natural persons may export payment instruments granted under the exchange regulations; foreign-banknote export must occur within 30 days of grant of the FX allocation, failing which the currency must be surrendered/re-sold, and departure requires the change slip and/or debit advice from an eligible FX/convertible-dirham account. Foreign non-residents and Moroccans residing abroad may export foreign-currency payment instruments previously imported, with foreign banknotes / bearer negotiable instruments requiring the relevant Customs declaration and inbound-import proof. Art. 40 also imposes an exit Customs declaration when covered effects / means of payment / bearer negotiable instruments equal or exceed MAD 100,000 (>=), kept separate from resident allocation rules and non-resident re-export provenance. Separately, Art. 41 provides a special MRE repurchase path: MRE may repurchase from banks/authorised exchange operators and export foreign currency previously repatriated and sold on the FX market during the previous 12 months, subject to the article's annual ceiling and documentation — not to be collapsed into ordinary non-resident re-export. Physical MAD banknotes remain under Art. 42 (<= MAD 2,000).

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Under IGOC 2026 Art. 38, foreign-currency payment instruments imported by residents, regardless of amount, must generally be surrendered to banks, authorised currency-exchange operators or authorised sub-delegates within a period not exceeding 30 days from entry. Within that window, foreign residents and exporters of goods and/or services may credit qualifying foreign banknotes to eligible FX/convertible-dirham accounts (Arts 90, 98 and/or 228 as applicable). Foreign residents may also hold, without that banknote surrender clock, specified non-banknote instruments issued abroad (traveller's cheques, bank/postal cheques, letters of credit, payment cards and similar) where Art. 38 so provides. Separately, Art. 140 defines eligible personal-travel beneficiaries; Art. 141 sets the numeric allowance — base MAD 100,000 plus a supplement equal to 30% of prior-year income tax paid/withheld, total not exceeding MAD 500,000 per person per calendar year; Art. 142 governs payment modalities (banks, exchange operators, cards, agency paths). These rules do not establish a universal resident right to hold any foreign-currency product, nor a blanket prohibition on all resident FX holding.

non_resident_rules.label: Non-resident rules
non_resident_rules.text: Under IGOC 2026 Art. 38, natural-person non-residents may exchange imported foreign currency for MAD or retain it and exchange it progressively according to their needs. For qualifying foreign-investment operations, non-residents may pay in foreign banknotes within six months of entry into eligible Art. 228 FX/convertible-dirham accounts. Do not collapse foreign residents (Art. 38 resident limb / account qualifications) with non-residents. Banks are authorised under Art. 228 to open FX and convertible-dirham accounts for: foreign natural persons (resident or non-resident); Moroccans residing abroad; foreign legal persons and their representations; industrial acceleration-zone companies; offshore financial-centre entities; diplomatic representations; and international organisations and their representations. Credits may include incoming foreign transfers, transfers from eligible FX/convertible-dirham accounts, and qualifying instruments; foreign-banknote deposits require the inbound declaration (generally within six months) or other specified proof. Debits cover qualifying transfers, FX-market sales and withdrawals under the article. Account eligibility is not unrestricted convertibility of every source of funds. Exporter accounts are separate (Arts 90 and 98).

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out
take_foreign_currency_out.text: On exit, individuals transporting cash or negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 or its equivalent shall declare them to the Nigeria Customs Service (statutory operator >). A person who falsely declares or fails to declare as required commits an offence and is liable on conviction to forfeiture of the undeclared funds or negotiable instrument, or to imprisonment for a term of at least two years, or both. Separately and narrowly, where foreign currency in excess of US$10,000 is imported in cash (not by bank draft, mail, or telegraphic transfer) and deposited in a domiciliary account with an authorised dealer, withdrawals from that account may be made only in cash and that imported cash is exportable from Nigeria only in cash (FEMMPA s.21). This field does not treat the amount declared on entry as a universal outbound ceiling, and it does not impose a general authorised-dealer-document requirement on every departing traveller.

exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Describe remaining regulatory mechanisms, not a severity score. Under FEMMPA, CBN may issue Market guidelines (with Ministerial approval) governing transaction procedures. CBN may appoint Authorised Dealers and Authorised Buyers; Market transactions run through the statutory public/AD/AB channels. Market foreign-exchange purchases require appropriate documentation except where a transaction is prohibited by law and subject to section 11(b). Authorised Dealers issue Certificates of Capital Importation and make related returns to CBN for qualifying inward investment. Any person may open and maintain a foreign-currency domiciliary account with an Authorised Dealer, subject to financial-institution identification evidence for opening or wholesale cash/inter-bank funding. Individuals must declare cash or negotiable instruments in excess of US$10,000 on entry and exit. Physical naira import and export remain prohibited except as permitted under Central Bank guidelines. Separately, CBN, with the Financial Markets Dealers Association, regulates the EFEMS system and publishes guidelines, rules, and real-time data for FX Code and Market Operating Guidelines compliance. These are discrete regulated mechanisms; this field does not classify Nigeria as fully liberalised or invent a current intervention modality.

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Any person may open, maintain and operate a foreign-currency domiciliary account with an Authorised Dealer. The account may be denominated in any internationally convertible currency, and a person may open more than one domiciliary account in the same or different currencies and at the same or different banks. Except as provided under any other enactment or law, an applicant to open a domiciliary account under FEMMPA is not obliged to disclose the source of the foreign currency sought to be deposited. Exporters of goods, including petroleum products, must open and maintain a separate foreign-currency domiciliary account for export proceeds — a class distinct from ordinary domiciliary accounts. Where a customer opens a domiciliary account or makes a wholesale cash or inter-bank deposit, the financial institution must obtain appropriate identification evidence (and, for inter-bank funding, satisfy itself that the transferring institution is regulated for ML/TF/PF prevention). Identification / KYC requirements are not treated here as a general prior CBN approval rule for resident foreign-currency accounts.

non_resident_rules.label: Non-resident rules
non_resident_rules.text: Non-resident treatment is category-specific. For external and non-resident non-Nigerian customers, financial institutions must confirm permanent residence outside Nigeria; eligible external-account classes include embassies, high commissions, legations or consulates and their career/established members, and other internationally recognised organisations accorded diplomatic status and their expatriate officials. Separate eligible non-resident-account classes include overseas correspondence and examination bodies, foreign companies executing approved contracts in Nigeria, and foreign professional bodies. Accounts under CDD Regulation 25 subregulations (2) and (4) shall, on completion of the contract or the applicant’s business in Nigeria, be closed and any balance transferred to the customer’s account in the country of residence after proper documentation. Cases not classified under those eligible classes are referred to the Central Bank for clarification — a referral rule, not a universal non-resident CBN-approval requirement. Separately, from 1 January 2025 eligible Non-Resident Nigerians may own a Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account (NRNOA) or Non-Resident Nigerian Investment Account (NRNIA) subject to KYC, without prejudice to Memorandum 17 of the CBN Foreign Exchange Manual (2018). NRNOA supports remittance of foreign earnings and dual-currency management; NRNIA supports investment in Nigerian assets. NRNOA foreign-currency balances may be fully repatriated out of Nigeria without restriction under the NRNOA-specific rule; NRNOA Naira accounts may be funded by offshore remittance or conversion from a foreign-currency account through authorised dealers. Do not project NRNOA/NRNIA rights onto all foreign persons or entities, and do not merge the two account classes.

banking_conversion_practicality.label: Banking & channels
banking_conversion_practicality.text: The Central Bank may appoint Authorised Dealers and Authorised Buyers of foreign currency subject to appointment terms. Market transactions occur between the public and Authorised Dealers, among Authorised Dealers, and between Authorised Dealers and Authorised Buyers. Each Market transaction rate is the rate mutually agreed between the applicant purchaser and the Authorised Dealer or Authorised Buyer concerned. FEMMPA section 11 provides that nothing in the Act permits unrestrained or general dealing in foreign currencies on terms inconsistent with the Act, or Market transactions relating to goods, services, or items absolutely prohibited by law — a statutory construction boundary, not commentary on scarcity or delay. Eligible NFEM transactions such as medical needs, school fees, BTA/PTA, and SME transactions are processed by Deposit Money Banks under CBN’s non-exhaustive ‘such as’ framing. This field does not assert bank-only conversion for every FX need and does not add availability, scarcity, or rate-quality commentary.

bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: Under CDSA 1992 s60(1), a person must not move or attempt to move into Singapore cash whose total value exceeds the prescribed amount (or its foreign-currency equivalent) without giving the required report. CBNI Regulations 2007 reg 2A prescribe that amount as S$20,000 — operator exceeds / strictly greater than S$20,000, not 'S$20,000 or more'. For ordinary traveller movements into Singapore, reg 3 generally requires Form NP 727 within 72 hours before immigration clearance on arrival (air/land/train/sea and related traveller subparagraphs; other manners and cargo/postal paths use distinct timing/forms including NP 728 where applicable). ICA operational guidance requires electronic NP 727 submission to SPF (e-727 / MyICA / SGAC). Definitions are pinned to CDSA s59: 'cash' means physical currency or a bearer negotiable instrument; 'physical currency' means coin and printed money that is designated as legal tender and circulates as a medium of exchange; 'bearer negotiable instrument' means a traveller's cheque or any negotiable instrument in bearer form, indorsed without restriction, made out to a fictitious payee, or otherwise in such form that title passes upon delivery, and includes a negotiable instrument signed with the payee's name omitted. ICA confirms there is no maximum amount or type restriction on bringing CBNI into Singapore. Contravention of s60(1) is an offence under s60(2) (fine not exceeding S$50,000 or imprisonment not exceeding 3 years or both); ICA also notes possible seizure/confiscation. This is an AML/crime-control disclosure regime under Part 6A, not an ECA capital-control ceiling.

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out

For ordinary traveller movements leaving Singapore, reg 4 generally requires Form NP 727 within 72 hours before immigration clearance on departure (transport-specific subparagraphs apply). ICA requires electronic NP 727 to SPF and states there is no maximum amount or type of CBNI that may be taken out; the S$20,000 figure is a reporting trigger only. exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Singapore's Exchange Control Act 1953 remains legally in force. Exchange Control (Continuance of Act) Notification 2023 (S 847/2023) s2, made under ECA s1(3), extends the period during which the Act remains in force through 31 December 2033. ECA s33 provides that obligations/prohibitions have effect subject to exemptions granted by order of the Authority (absolute or conditional). ECA s38 authorises general or special permission, consent or authority (revocable, absolute or conditional) and directions. MAS Notice 1103 / Circular (title: Exchange Control Liberalisation; reference ID Circular 6/78 dd 25.5.78; dated 25 May 1978; effective 1 June 1978) — operative text as quoted in Focus Energy Ltd v Aye Aye Soe [2010] SGHC 48 [9] — exempts all persons from ECA provisions/obligations so that no exchange-control formalities or approvals are required for payments or capital transfers, and abolishes prior Exchange Control Manual limits. The Court held at [11]-[13] that MAS lawfully exercised ss33 and 38 powers, and at [14]-[15] that ECA prohibitions have been effectively suspended for relevant payments since 1 June 1978 until the Circular is revoked or modified; [16] applies that holding. Exemption currentness sweep of the reviewed official corpus (current ECA; ECA subsidiary-legislation list showing only S 847/2023; MAS Notice 1103 page with no amendment notes; Focus Energy) located no official revocation or narrowing of that blanket exemption. This is not a statement that the ECA was repealed, nor a claim of active broad capital controls, nor a denial of AML/CBNI, licensing or sanctions layers. Absence of a located revocation is not evidence that no special or future restriction can exist.

A traveller may make a voluntary declaration, and Turkish Customs may require an explanation and documentation of the amount, its source and its purpose under the anti-money-laundering framework (Law No. 5549) — an onboarding/compliance explanation layer, not the legal source of the import freedom. Separately, certain cash categories are, by reason of source or purpose, not permitted to be carried into Türkiye by passengers and must instead move through the banking system (Ministry of Trade Cash Controls Circular). The reviewed sources do not establish a symmetric inbound EUR 10,000 declaration ceiling.

take_foreign_currency_out.label: Taking currency out
take_foreign_currency_out.text: Taking cash out of Türkiye is declaration-triggered. Carrying Turkish lira exceeding (aşan) TRY 185,000 out of the country requires a declaration on the Customs Cash Declaration Form (Nakit Beyan Formu) (Decree No. 32 Art. 3(d); Communiqué No. 2008-32/34 Art. 3(5)). Carrying foreign banknotes (efektif) exceeding EUR 10,000 or the equivalent in other foreign currency out of the country likewise requires a Nakit Beyan Formu declaration (Decree No. 32 Art. 4(f); Communiqué No. 2008-32/34 Art. 4(2)). The binding word is 'aşan' (exceeding, strictly '>'). These figures are declaration triggers, not a maximum exportable amount; separately, certain cash categories may not be carried out by passengers by reason of source or purpose and must move through the banking system. The pre-March-2025 TRY 25,000 figure is superseded and is not used.

cash_declaration_threshold.label: Declaration threshold
cash_declaration_threshold.text: On exit the cross-border cash-declaration triggers are: Turkish lira exceeding TRY 185,000, and foreign banknotes (efektif) exceeding EUR 10,000 or the equivalent — in each case declared to Turkish Customs on the Cash Declaration Form (Nakit Beyan Formu). The binding operator is 'exceeding' (aşan, strictly '>'). On entry there is no general mandatory numeric declaration threshold: foreign-currency import is generally free under Decree No. 32 Art. 4(a), declaration is voluntary, and Customs may require an explanation of amount, source and purpose under Law No. 5549 as a compliance layer. Legal basis: Decree No. 32 (Art. 3(d), Art. 4(f)) and Communiqué No. 2008-32/34 (Art. 3(5), Art. 4(2)); enforcement by the Ministry of Trade / Turkish Customs (Customs Law No. 4458). This customs declaration is distinct from the banking-channel-only cash categories, from the anti-money-laundering explanation layer, and from any notion of an export ceiling.

exchange_controls.label: Exchange controls
exchange_controls.text: Türkiye does not operate a single general exchange-control authorisation regime in the reviewed sources; instead several distinct, layered elements apply and must not be conflated: a floating exchange-rate regime with no target (CBRT), kept separate from controls; generally liberal foreign-exchange holding by residents (Art. 4(b)) and FX deposit-account opening for residents and non-residents (Art. 19(1)); transfers abroad through banks (Art. 4(e)); outbound physical-cash declaration triggers (Turkish lira exceeding TRY 185,000; efektif exceeding EUR 10,000 — Nakit Beyan Formu); source/purpose cash categories that must move through the banking system; a restriction on foreign-currency-denominated domestic contracts (Art. 4(g)); an export-proceeds repatriation/surrender regime under the CBRT Export Circular; and transaction-specific capital-movement and reporting rules. Bank-level macroprudential foreign-exchange measures (reserve requirements, conversion incentives) are prudential rules applied to banks and are not customer currency-passage restrictions. The reviewed sources do not establish that Türkiye is 'fully liberalised' or has 'no controls', and absence of a located restriction is not evidence that none exists.

resident_holding_rules.label: Resident rules
resident_holding_rules.text: Under Decree No. 32 Art. 4(b), persons resident in Türkiye (Türkiye'de yerleşik kişiler — Decree Art. 2) may generally possess foreign exchange, buy and sell foreign exchange through authorised channels, hold foreign exchange in bank foreign-currency (döviz tevdiat) accounts, hold and use foreign banknotes (efektif), and dispose of foreign exchange through banks domestically and abroad. Separately, Decree No. 32 Art. 19(1) provides that the Central Bank and banks may open foreign-currency deposit accounts (döviz tevdiat hesapları) and precious-metal depot accounts in the name of persons resident in Türkiye; account holders may freely dispose of those accounts; interest is freely agreed between bank and account holder; and principal and interest transfers are met by banks from their own resources. Art. 4(b) is the resident FX possession/use/holding layer; Art. 19(1) is the FX deposit-account opening and disposition framework. Neither provision is a Central Bank approval regime for ordinary holding, and neither establishes an unconditional right to every banking product or service. Customer-due-diligence / KYC obligations are a separate operational/compliance onboarding layer and are not the legal source of this account framework. Transaction-specific rules (for example on foreign-currency-denominated domestic contracts or reporting) may separately apply.

non_resident_rules.label: Non-resident rules
non_resident_rules.text: Under Decree No. 32 Art. 4(d), persons resident abroad (Dışarıda yerleşik kişiler — Decree Art. 2) may buy and sell foreign exchange with banks, authorised institutions (yetkili müesseseler), the PTT, precious-metal intermediary institutions and brokerages. Under Art. 4(e), persons resident in Türkiye and persons resident abroad may freely cause foreign-exchange transfers abroad through banks. Separately, Decree No. 32 Art. 19(1) provides that the Central Bank and banks may open foreign-currency deposit accounts (döviz tevdiat hesapları) and precious-metal depot accounts in the name of persons resident abroad; account holders may freely dispose of those accounts; interest is freely agreed between bank and account holder; and principal and interest transfers are met by banks from their own resources. This is the FX deposit-account opening framework for non-residents — not a claim that non-residents 'transfer more freely', and not an unconditional right to every Turkish-lira or foreign-currency banking product. Customer-due-diligence / KYC obligations remain a separate operational/compliance onboarding layer. Transaction-specific restrictions and reporting may separately apply.

bring_foreign_currency_in.label: Bringing currency in
bring_foreign_currency_in.text: Inbound travellers may carry foreign currency without a legislated statutory cap analogous to rigid import licences. When the traveller carries currencies, cheque-like bearer forms, jewellery, or precious metals whose combined declarable valuation exceeds AED 60,000, UAE customs doctrine expects a declaration aligned with traveller-transparency publications and ICP-aligned digital facilitation at covered ports. Household members under eighteen are not ordinarily required to lodge a standalone declaration beyond inclusion on a guardian declaration where facts support that treatment. Omitting mandated declarations where threshold facts exist is prosecuted as customs evasion risk rather than a routine paperwork preference.

This traveller border report is distinct from Bank Secrecy Act filings by financial institutions — Currency Transaction Reports (CTR) and Suspicious Activity Reports (SAR) — and from Foreign Bank Account Reports (FBAR); none of those is a traveller declaration.
